hints: Calculate the driving force at $v = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ using $F = \frac{P}{v}$.
Apply Newton's second law horizontally: $F - R = ma$.
Substitute $m = 80\text{ kg}$ and $a = 0.3\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to verify $R = 16\text{ N}$.
walkthrough:
State the formula relating power, driving force, and speed:
$$P = F \times v \implies F = \frac{P}{v}$$
Substitute $P = 240\text{ W}$ and $v = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F = \frac{240}{6} = 40\text{ N}$$

State Newton's second law for the cyclist in the direction of motion:
$$\Sigma F = ma \implies F - R = ma$$
Substitute $F = 40\text{ N}$, $m = 80\text{ kg}$, and $a = 0.3\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$40 - R = 80 \times 0.3$$
$$80 \times 0.3 = 24$$
$$40 - R = 24$$

Rearrange to solve for the resistance $R$:
$$R = 40 - 24 = 16\text{ N}$$

hints: At steady speed, acceleration is zero, so the driving force equals resistance: $F = 16\text{ N}$.
walkthrough:
State the condition for maintaining a constant steady speed ($a = 0$):
$$\Sigma F = 0 \implies F_D - R = 0 \implies F_D = R = 16\text{ N}$$

Use the power formula to determine the speed:
$$P = F_D \times v \implies v = \frac{P}{F_D}$$
Substitute $P = 240\text{ W}$ and $F_D = 16\text{ N}$:
$$v = \frac{240}{16} = \frac{30}{2} = 15\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

hints: Calculate the driving force at $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$: $F = \frac{240}{4} = 60\text{ N}$.
Identify the forces opposing motion up the slope: resistance ($16\text{ N}$) and the downhill component of weight ($mg\sin 3^\circ$).
Apply Newton's second law along the slope: $60 - 16 - 80g\sin 3^\circ = 80a$.
walkthrough:
Determine the driving force provided by the cyclist at $v = 4\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{240}{4} = 60\text{ N}$$

Identify the forces acting parallel to the $3^\circ$ inclined plane:
- Up the slope: Driving force $F_D = 60\text{ N}$.
- Down the slope: Resistance $R = 16\text{ N}$.
- Down the slope: Component of gravity $W_x = mg\sin 3^\circ = 80 \times 10 \times \sin 3^\circ = 800\sin 3^\circ$.

State Newton's second law along the incline:
$$\Sigma F_{\text{parallel}} = ma$$
$$F_D - R - mg\sin 3^\circ = ma$$
$$60 - 16 - 800\sin 3^\circ = 80a$$
$$44 - 800\sin 3^\circ = 80a$$

Calculate the numerical values:
$$\sin 3^\circ \approx 0.0523360$$
$$800 \times 0.0523360 \approx 41.8688\text{ N}$$
$$44 - 41.8688 = 2.1312\text{ N}$$
$$a = \frac{2.1312}{80} \approx 0.02664\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $a = 0.0266\text{ m s}^{-2}$ up the hill.
